git.title: Git
git.summary: Distributed version control used to clone, update, and manage the dotfiles repositories.
git.why: Core bootstrap dependency and the source-control layer for every managed machine.

tmux.title: tmux
tmux.summary: Terminal multiplexer for persistent sessions, panes, and resilient remote workflows.
tmux.why: Keeps the same terminal workspace available locally and over SSH.

curl.title: curl
curl.summary: Command-line data transfer tool used for HTTPS bootstrap and artifact retrieval.
curl.why: Provides the smallest broadly available path for fetching the public installer and verified artifacts.

tar.title: GNU tar
tar.summary: Archive utility used to unpack release artifacts and portable tool fallbacks.
tar.why: Needed by the bootstrap path when a package is acquired as a verified archive.

stow.title: GNU Stow
stow.summary: Symlink farm manager that maps repository packages into the home directory.
stow.why: The sole configuration deployment authority, keeping changes reversible and inspectable.

just.title: just
just.summary: Command runner that exposes memorable dotfiles recipes without owning installer logic.
just.why: Adds discoverable commands and shell completions while keeping the underlying CLI authoritative.

openssh.title: OpenSSH
openssh.summary: SSH client and tooling for secure remote shell access.
openssh.why: Required on Termux and remote-oriented machines so the terminal environment can follow you across hosts.

zsh.title: Zsh
zsh.summary: Interactive Unix shell with strong completion and customization support.
zsh.why: One of the supported interactive shells for a consistent local terminal experience.

helix.title: Helix
helix.summary: Modal terminal editor with built-in tree-sitter, LSP, and multiple-selection workflows.
helix.why: Primary terminal-native editor across development, remote, Linux, and mobile roles.

yazi.title: Yazi
yazi.summary: Fast terminal file manager with previews, tabs, async I/O, and keyboard-first navigation.
yazi.why: Provides the same filesystem workflow on local, remote, and mobile terminals.

starship.title: Starship
starship.summary: Cross-shell prompt that surfaces repository, runtime, and system context.
starship.why: Keeps prompt information consistent across supported shells and machines.

atuin.title: Atuin
atuin.summary: Searchable shell history stored in a structured local database with optional encrypted sync.
atuin.why: Replaces fragile reverse-search history with contextual search across managed shells.

zoxide.title: zoxide
zoxide.summary: Frequency-aware directory jumper that learns the paths used most often.
zoxide.why: Makes navigation consistent and fast without maintaining hand-written directory aliases.

eza.title: eza
eza.summary: Modern replacement for ls with better defaults, metadata, Git state, and tree views.
eza.why: Improves everyday directory inspection in the portable shell layer.

bat.title: bat
bat.summary: Syntax-highlighted cat replacement with paging, line numbers, and Git-aware output.
bat.why: Used for readable file previews, manuals, and fuzzy-finder previews.

fd.title: fd
fd.summary: Fast, user-friendly filesystem search tool with sensible defaults and regex support.
fd.why: Supports editor, shell, and file-manager search flows without verbose find syntax.

ripgrep.title: ripgrep
ripgrep.summary: Recursive text search optimized for speed while respecting ignore files by default.
ripgrep.why: Core search primitive for development, editor, and remote workflows.

gh.title: GitHub CLI
gh.summary: Official GitHub command-line client for authentication, repositories, pull requests, and API workflows.
gh.why: Acts as the authentication gateway from the safe public bootstrap to the private dotfiles overlay.

lazygit.title: lazygit
lazygit.summary: Terminal UI for common Git staging, history, branch, merge, and rebase operations.
lazygit.why: Provides a fast interactive Git surface without replacing Git itself.

fnm.title: fnm
fnm.summary: Fast Node.js version manager with per-shell and per-project version switching.
fnm.why: Keeps Node runtimes explicit and isolated for development machines.

btop.title: btop
btop.summary: Interactive resource monitor for CPU, memory, disks, network, and processes.
btop.why: Desktop role monitor for quickly understanding machine pressure and runaway processes.

fastfetch.title: Fastfetch
fastfetch.summary: Fast system-information summary for OS, hardware, shell, terminal, and runtime context.
fastfetch.why: Useful for workstation diagnostics and quickly confirming which environment is active.

gdu.title: gdu
gdu.summary: Fast disk-usage analyzer with an interactive terminal interface.
gdu.why: Desktop role utility for finding large directories and storage regressions quickly.

lnav.title: lnav
lnav.summary: Log-file navigator that merges, tails, searches, filters, and queries structured logs in the terminal.
lnav.why: Provides a richer inspection surface for development and workstation troubleshooting.

htop.title: htop
htop.summary: Interactive process viewer for CPU, memory, process trees, signals, and priorities.
htop.why: Server role fallback that is widely packaged and usable over constrained remote shells.

rclone.title: Rclone
rclone.summary: Command-line file synchronization and transfer across local storage and many cloud providers.
rclone.why: Server role tool for backups, transfers, and remote storage operations without a desktop client.

jq.title: jq
jq.summary: Streaming JSON processor for querying, transforming, and composing structured command output.
jq.why: macOS public baseline utility for reliable JSON inspection and scripting.
